caption: The power button on a remote pointed at a television is pressed, and the screen lights up.

sa.check: A television with a dark screen.
A remote is pointed at the television.
The power button on the remote is pressed.
The remote is aimed at the television, not elsewhere.
The order is dark, press, lit.

pc.expect: The screen comes on at or just after the press, and only then.
pc.fail: The button is pressed and the screen stays dark to the end of the clip; or the screen is lit before the press; or the screen comes on while the remote lies untouched; or the screen comes on while the remote points away from the television.

pc.expect: Once on, the screen stays on for the rest of the clip and shows a steady picture or menu.
pc.fail: The screen goes dark again by itself; or flickers on and off; or the picture appears and shrinks back to black; or the screen turns on and off with each frame.

pc.expect: The screen's glow reaches its surroundings: the wall behind and the shelf beneath brighten with the screen, and the standby light, if any, changes state at the press.
pc.fail: The screen is lit while the room around it stays as dark as before; or the room brightens while the screen stays dark; or the standby light stays as it was while the screen comes on.

pc.expect: The television and the remote stay where they are, apart from the hand's movement; nothing else in the room moves at the press.
pc.fail: The television shifts or turns at the press; or the remote moves with no hand on it; or objects on the shelf jump.

pc.expect: One television and one remote; the television keeps its shape; the hand passes through nothing.
pc.fail: A second screen or remote appears; or the television vanishes; or the remote passes through the hand; or the television changes size or shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The television's frame, the remote's buttons and the room stay the same apart from the screen.
pc.fail: The frame changes colour; or the remote's button layout changes; or the room's contents rearrange.

note: The picture that appears on the screen is not judged; any content counts as lit.
